newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African metal industry wage talks set to resume.
newsitem.headline: S.African metal industry wage talks set to resume.

text.p: Employers and trade unions in the metal industry on Wednesday agreed to resume wage talks after the parties deadlocked earlier this month, the Steel and Engineering Industries Federation of South Africa (Seifsa) said.
"Both parties agreed to meet on Tuesday July 1, 1997 in a smaller negotiating forum to discuss the various issues currently in dispute," employer body Seifsa said in a statement.
At a meeting on June 12, employers tabled a final wage offer of between eight and 8.5 percent together with other improved offers on conditions of employment which unions rejected.

A number of unions, including the Congress of South African Trade Unions-affilated National Union of Metalworkers of South Africa and the Chemical Workers' Industrial Union subsequently declared a dispute with employers.

Other unions in dispute are the National Employees' Trade Union, the Mine Workers' Union, the SA Workers' Union, the Metal and Electrical Workers" Union of SA, the SA Electrical Workers' Association and the Radio, Television, Electronics and Allied Workers' Union.
Employers declared a counter-dispute against the trade unions.
Unions are demanding wage increases ranging from 13 to 23 percent.
